_doc: Jev site for bank and card alerts (lib/bank-alert-judge.mjs, called by bin/plaid-sync once per run). One question per candidate transaction, asked after lib/bank-alert-research.mjs has gathered what Jori already knows about it (ledger facts, the property books' entry, memory, mail carrying the same amount): is it worth interrupting the user about? A candidate is a new posted transaction at or above the alert size (finance.json `alerts`) that code did not already pair as the user's own money moving between two linked accounts. Legacy (fallback below the threshold, and shadow during a shadow window) is a toolless Sonnet judgment built from this file's wording. When the answer is yes, Sonnet writes the chat message (one per run): the raw bank line never goes to chat. Kernel definition; an installation's own data/jev-questions/bank-alert.json replaces it.

alert.instructions: `item` is a new transaction in one of {{owner_name}}'s linked bank or card accounts, big enough to be considered for an alert. `item.transaction` is the transaction (direction in = money arriving, out = money leaving; `description` is the bank's own line). `item.account` is the account it hit. `item.similar_history` lists earlier posted transactions in the SAME account, same direction, within about 20% of this amount, over the past 13 months (date, amount, description): a match in description and size means it has happened before. `item.merchant_history` summarizes earlier charges at the same merchant (count and largest), null when there is no merchant or no history. `item.nearby_same_amount` lists other transactions of exactly this amount within a few days in any linked account; a pending copy of this same transaction can appear there and is not a second event. `item.own_transfer_match` is true only when code found the matching other leg in another linked account. `item.old_rule` is what the previous fixed-threshold rule would have done. `linked_accounts` is every account the assistant can see (name, last 4 digits, type). `item.research` is what the assistant already knows about it, gathered before this question: `ledger` holds {{owner_name}}'s own recorded finance facts (`recorded_verdict` = they already explained this exact transaction; `expected_income_on_this_account` and `scheduled_payments_on_this_account` = income or payments they told the assistant to expect here, with the payer text to look for and the usual amount; `invoice_payment_match` and `open_invoices` = invoices this pays or could pay; `security_deposit_movement` and `security_deposits_held_in_this_account` = tenant security deposits); `books` is the property books' own entry (category, property, the classifier's reason, a matched receipt); `memory` is what {{owner_name}} said in chat or replies, wiki notes and indexed mail about this payee; `email` is mail from around that date carrying this exact amount (a payout notice, an invoice, a wire or transfer confirmation). Research the transaction through these before answering: when any of them explains it (a recorded verdict, expected income or a scheduled payment whose payer and size fit, an invoice it settles, a deposit refund or payout to a tenant, a receipt, an email that announces or confirms it, something {{owner_name}} said), it is expected and not worth an interruption, however large. Should {{owner_name}} be interrupted about this transaction right now? Yes only when nothing in the research or history explains it and money leaves to a payee or account not seen before, or to an account that is not one of `linked_accounts` and has no history of such transfers; when a charge is new or clearly larger than what is usual for that payee; when a deposit is from an unfamiliar source or clearly unusual in size; when it looks like fraud, an error, a duplicate charge, or a fee or penalty; or when a large amount moves in a way the history does not explain. No when it is routine and expected: rent, payroll or other income from a payer seen before at a similar amount, a recurring bill in line with its history, a regular transfer the history shows happening before, a card payment, the other side of a move between two linked accounts, or a pending copy of something already posted. When the history clearly shows it as a regular event, it is not worth an interruption even if the amount is large.

criteria.true: after checking the research and the history, nothing explains it: it is unexpected, new, unusual in size or destination, or looks wrong, so {{owner_name}} would want to know now
criteria.false: the research or the history explains it: a recorded fact, expected income or a scheduled payment, an invoice it settles, a tenant deposit movement, a matched receipt or email, something the user said, a regular event, or the user's own money moving between linked accounts
